title: authzLimitedClient must reject checks a service token cannot delegate before forwarding them
answers: Do I need to call serviceCanDelegate before the underlying authz client?
What must Check/Compile/BatchCheck do before forwarding to the real client?
How is a deployment misconfiguration distinguished from a normal access denial?
body:
Every entry point on authzLimitedClient (Check, Compile, BatchCheck in pkg/storage/unified/resource/access.go) must call serviceCanDelegate(ctx, id, group, resource, verb) before forwarding the check to the underlying authz client. This is the layer that decides which kinds get access-checked, so it's the only place that can tell 'service token misconfigured' apart from 'user genuinely denied'.
If skipped: a service whose token has permissions but not the delegated one for that group/resource/verb will get a silent local denial from authlib, and the caller sees empty/unauthorized results with no signal that anything is wrong (no log, no metric, no error).
The check is a no-op (returns nil) when the identity carries no token permissions at all (single-tenant/in-process callers), so it must not be tightened to reject those.
applies: pkg/storage/unified/resource/access.go — authzLimitedClient and any future entry points added to it
